extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners, European patent attorneys, applicants and other IP professionals involved in prosecution before the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Comprehensive Guidelines for Examination at the European Patent Office covering formalities, search, substantive examination, opposition/limitation/revocation, procedural matters, application content, patentability, and amendments/corrections under the EPC. Used to evaluate and process European patent applications and proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of applications and examination on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements relating to filing a European patent application and the examination carried out at the filing stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part A, Chapter II for detailed formal filing requirements, which set out what is checked on filing and what defects may be raised or invited to be remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application meets the formal requirements prescribed by the EPC and implementing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part A, Chapter III for lists of formal requirements, how defects are communicated, and how corrections/amendments at the formalities stage are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating the formalities report; amendment of application; correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: How formalities reports are issued and how applicants may amend or correct mistakes in the application in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on issuing reports, permissible amendments/corrections at this stage, time limits and procedure (Part A, Chapter V).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of application; request for examination and transmission of the dossier to Examining Division
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing publication of the application, requesting substantive examination, and when the dossier is passed to the Examining Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part A, Chapter VI for timing, formalities, and consequences for the start of substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Language requirements for filing, proceedings and translations under the EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A, Chapter VII covers acceptable languages, translation obligations, and effects of language deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and substantive requirements for drawings submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A, Chapter IX details required format, clarity, and consequences of non-compliant drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment requirements, fee types, timetables, and consequences of non-payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A, Chapter X sets out how fees must be paid, reductions, surcharges and default remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of files; communication of information contained in files; consultation of the Register of European Patents; issuance of certified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to file contents, register consultation and issuance of certified documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part A, Chapter XI explains public and private access rights, how to obtain certified copies and how information is communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative standards describing what a proper prior-art search should aim to achieve at the search stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter III outlines expectations for completeness, relevance, limits of the search and how the searcher's work is characterised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search procedure and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology and strategy expected for conducting the prior-art search (databases, keywords, classifications, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter IV provides procedural guidance on search approach, use of classifications and selection of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclassification (routing) and official classification of European patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: How applications are routed and classified to assist searching and examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter V explains preclassification steps and the official classification system used by the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: The state of the art at the search stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and scope of the 'state of the art' relevant for the search and which documents should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter VI clarifies temporal and content limits for what counts as prior art at the search stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application satisfies the requirement of unity of invention for search purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter VII explains criteria for unity, when partial searches are appropriate, and how lack of unity is handled during search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter to be excluded from the search
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of subject-matter that are not to be searched (e.g., non-technical content, excluded biological material as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter VIII lists exclusions and explains rationale and procedure for excluding subject-matter from the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and formats for documenting the search, including how cited prior art is recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter IX sets out how search documentation should be prepared to support the search report and later examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and structure of the European search report to be issued to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter X describes which documents must be cited, classifications, and explanatory text to be included in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: The search opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The searcher's opinion accompanying the search report, giving preliminary views on patentability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B, Chapter XI explains the scope, purpose and typical content of the search opinion and its use by examiners and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements to be met before the Division starts substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and formalities that must be fulfilled prior to initiating substantive examination by the Examining Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter II lists prerequisites (e.g., fee payment, translations, request for examination) and consequences if unmet.

rubrics_metrics.name: The first stage of substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial substantive checks and procedures undertaken when substantive examination begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter III covers search result consideration, checking of claims vs. description, and initial objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of replies and further stages of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: How examiner evaluates applicant's replies and the subsequent iterative examination steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter IV provides guidance on admissibility of amendments in replies, further objections, and procedural handling of interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The final stage of substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedure for concluding substantive examination, grant or refusal decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter V explains requirements for grantability, final communications, and preparing decision text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and acceleration of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on applicable time limits during examination and mechanisms for accelerated processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter VI details statutory and procedural time limits, extension/reduction provisions and acceleration schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other procedures in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Various additional procedural aspects that may arise during substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part C, Chapter VII addresses specific procedural variants and exceptional measures during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (application content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of unity of invention as it applies to the content of the application (distinct from search-stage treatment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter V provides tests for unity when evaluating claims together with the description and when deciding on restriction/divisional application needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of a European patent application (other than claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the description, abstract and other parts of the application excluding claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter II enumerates required content, form and level of disclosure for description and abstract (see also annexes and checklist for abstracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for considering the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for what the abstract should contain and how it should be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter II – Annex 1 provides a checklist of items to be covered in an abstract (formatting, conciseness, essential features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the invention be disclosed sufficiently clearly and completely for it to be carried out by a skilled person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter III describes the test for sufficiency, what constitutes enablement, relevant examples and consequences of insufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims (Art. 84 and formal requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for claim wording, clarity, support by the description (Art.84), and other formal claim requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter IV sets out claim drafting requirements, common defects, how to assess clarity/conciseness/support and includes an annex with examples concerning essential features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for claiming priority, effect of priority dates and required evidence/documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F, Chapter VI explains entitlement, partial priorities, time limits and how priority affects novelty/ inventive step assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall standards determining whether subject-matter is patentable under the EPC framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter I frames the patentability assessment and the legal tests applied throughout Part G chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the invention be capable of industrial application (i.e., capable of being made or used in any kind of industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter III explains how industrial applicability is assessed and examples where it may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and boundaries of the prior art considered for novelty and inventive step assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter IV clarifies what counts as state of the art for patentability purposes and how to treat earlier disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances under which disclosures do not prejudice novelty (e.g., grace periods, certain exhibitions, mandated disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter V describes exceptions and conditions for non-prejudicial disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the claimed subject-matter is new over the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter VI sets out tests for novelty, how to compare claims with prior art documents, and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the claimed invention involve an inventive step (non-obviousness) over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G, Chapter VII contains the problem-solution approach, relevant indicators, and an annex with examples relating to the requirement of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and substantive examination of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and substantive standards for opposing a granted European patent, including how oppositions are examined and decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part D (Chapters II–V) covers the Opposition Division's role, grounds for opposition, substantive examination procedures, evidence handling and required determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions of the Opposition Division; costs; limitation and revocation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for decisions in opposition proceedings, allocation of costs and procedures for limitation or revocation of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part D, Chapters VIII–X set out decision-making criteria, cost rules and post-grant limitation/revocation procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and notifications; oral proceedings; evidence taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for communicating with parties, conducting oral proceedings and taking/conserving evidence in proceedings before the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E, Chapters I–III provide procedural rules on formal communications, conduct of hearings, admissibility and preservation of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits, loss of rights, further and accelerated processing and re-establishment of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on procedural time limits, consequences of missing them, options for accelerated processing, and re-establishment of rights in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E, Chapter VII describes applicable time limits, how loss of rights is treated, available remedies and acceleration mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: How PCT applications are processed at the EPO, interaction between PCT phases and European phase requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part E, Chapter VIII explains entering the European phase from a PCT application, required translations, time limits and effects on examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend; admissibility and allowability of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing the applicant's right to amend the application, admissibility of amendments (procedural) and allowability under Art.123(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H, Chapters I–IV set out who may amend, when amendments are admissible, tests for added subject-matter and extension of scope, and include examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correction of clerical or other errors in applications or proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H, Chapter VI details correction mechanisms, allowable corrections, and procedural requirements for effecting corrections.
